rule: Two kinds of fact, never merged. INTENT fields (intended_asin, official_listing_url, confirmation_date, confirmation_source) are filled only from an owner confirmation or an official Associates record; all four are blank here because none was supplied. OBSERVED fields (observed.*) are what an Amazon page served on a dated fetch. A blank intent field means 'not confirmed', never 'guessed'. Specs come from the manufacturer page named per field; where two official pages disagree the value is withheld and the flag says why.

products.fit_line: Two foods on two timers, in the footprint of one basket fryer.
products.lede: Two independent 3-quart baskets with a window on each, and a setting that lands both baskets at the same moment. The trade is that six quarts are two small drawers rather than one wide one.
products.best_for: Cooking two different foods that want different times, without heating the whole oven.
products.tradeoff: Each basket is 3 quarts, so a single big batch is split in two and a long item may not fit at all.

questions: Will both baskets really finish together?
Sync Finish is the manufacturer's own claim; there is no independent test of how close the two baskets land.
Can I see the food without opening it?
Yes — each basket has a viewing window, and the interior light is stated on the manufacturer page.
Does it fit under a cabinet?
10.63 in tall before the lid opens. Measure your clearance rather than trusting a photo.

questions: Does it replace a toaster oven and an air fryer?

Will a 12-inch pizza fit?

What is actually in the box?
The manufacturer's description says seven accessories; the listing title says six; the grill plate is sold separately on the manufacturer's own site. Ask the seller before ordering (CDF-06).

questions: Will a long item fit without cutting it?

How much counter depth does it need?

Do I have to learn a menu system?
No. Four presets plus manual time and temperature.

products.link_status: Provisional tagged link. Not yet validated in Associates Central (CDF-04).
products.fit_line: A one-second spot check you keep on the fridge door.
products.lede: A folding instant-read with a thermocouple at the tip, a rotating LED screen and a magnet on the back. It answers one question — is this piece done yet — and it answers it fast.
products.best_for: Checking several pieces of meat at the grill in a few seconds each.
products.tradeoff: It is a spot-check tool. The manufacturer's own manual says not to leave it in the oven, the microwave or the dishwasher, so it is not a leave-in probe.

probe.label: Probe
probe.value: 4.3 in long × 0.14 in at the base, tapering to 0.06 in

battery.label: Power
battery.value: One AAA cell; 30-second sleep; wake by movement

water.label: Water resistance
water.note: The manufacturer page states no IP number; the listing's IP67 is a marketplace claim and is not published here.

leave_in.label: Leave-in use
leave_in.note: The manual explicitly says not to leave it in food while cooking, so no leave-in rating is published.

warranty.label: Warranty
warranty.value: Lifetime warranty, activated by registration within 30 days

questions: How fast is a reading?
About one second, per the manufacturer, using a thermocouple rather than a thermistor.
Can I wash it under the tap?
The manufacturer says the design is waterproof but publishes no IP number. Wash and wipe; the manual says not to put it in a dishwasher.
Will it live in the drawer or on the fridge?
Either. The manual describes a magnet on the body and a fold-shut probe that puts the unit to sleep.

fit.fit_note: A drawer-sized handheld tool, so it is out of scope for the counter-space check.

products.link_status: Provisional tagged link. Not yet validated in Associates Central (CDF-04).
products.fit_line: Reports from inside three pieces of meat while the lid stays shut.
products.lede: Three slim probes, a hub that charges them and relays them over Wi-Fi, and an ambient sensor that watches the heat around the food as well as the food itself.
products.best_for: A long cook where you would rather not stand next to the grill, and where more than one piece of meat matters.
products.tradeoff: The inserted portion of the probe tops out at 212 °F. The 1,000 °F figure is the ambient sensor, not something you can put in hot oil. It also needs the app and the hub in the loop.

probes.label: Probes included
probes.note: The manufacturer sells one to four probes; this is the three-probe bundle

sensors.label: Sensors
sensors.value: 4 internal + 1 ambient, per the manufacturer page
sensors.note: The page also says 'Five Temperature Sensors' and the listing says '5 Sensors'; the split is stated in the feature list.

ambient_range.label: Ambient range
ambient_range.note: Gen 3 limit; the FAQ gives 752 °F for the earlier ambient sensor

connectivity.label: Connectivity
connectivity.value: Bluetooth probe-to-hub, Wi-Fi hub-to-app; USB-C charging; hub speaker

battery.label: Battery life
battery.note: The product page says '70+ hours'; the same brand's FAQ says up to 60 hours for Gen 3. Withheld (CDF-07).

cleanup.label: Cleanup
cleanup.value: Probe stated waterproof and dishwasher safe; the hub is not waterproof and should be wiped

warranty.label: Warranty
warranty.note: Not stated on the manufacturer product page or FAQ.

questions: Can I monitor from inside the house?
Yes. The hub relays over Wi-Fi rather than Bluetooth alone, which is what the unlimited-range claim rests on.
How many pieces of meat can I track at once?
Three with this bundle. The hub accepts up to four Gen 3 probes.
Will it survive a hot grill lid?
The ambient sensor is rated to 1,000 °F. The inserted portion is rated to 212 °F, which is a doneness range, not an oil-temperature range.

fit.fit_note: Probes and a hub that lives in a drawer or on a shelf, so it is out of scope for the counter-space check.
